'''Blessed Souls''' was a Star Wars CCG fan database at <code>blessed-souls.mine.sk</code> (a Slovak mine.sk host). The recovered homepage is titled '''SWCCG - Database'''. It listed championship years 1996–2007, player pages, deck pages, pictures, and movies, and named [[Players Committee]] (<code>swccgpc.com</code>) and a Holotable host as partners.<ref name="tco">[https://web.archive.org/web/20201114131040id_/https://t.co/RCNHte1tcY SWCCG - Database] (Wayback 14 November 2020 <code>id_</code> capture of t.co/RCNHte1tcY, which stored the destination HTML)</ref><ref name="tweet">[https://x.com/swccg/status/1327598657764356098 @swccg], 14 November 2020 (#swccg25to25, 2000 part 3/3)</ref>

The Players Committee X account pointed at that database for 2000 Worlds finalists’ decklists in the 14 November 2020 #swccg25to25 post (2000 part 3 of 3). The live hostname did not resolve under a matching certificate in 2026. Year pages linked from the homepage (1996–2007, including 2000 Worlds deck pages) have no Wayback CDX hits. The 2020 t.co snapshot is the surviving reading copy of the homepage.

A later capture of the same hostname is a different Slovak World of Warcraft guild also named Blessed Souls. That guild site is not this SWCCG database.

== What the recovered homepage had ==

Year navigation ran 1996 through 2007. Championship-name keywords on the homepage include [[Raphael Asselin]], [[Bjørn Sørgjerd]], [[Philipp Jacobs]], [[Michael Riboulet]], [[Matt Potter]], [[Gary Carman]], [[Steven Lewis]], [[Matt Sokol]], [[Yannick Lapointe]], [[Bastian Winkelhaus]], [[Martin Akesson]], [[Angelo Consoli]], [[Greg Shaw]], [[Jonny Chu]], [[Brandon Schele]], [[Reid Smith]], [[Drew Scott]], and [[James Booker]].

For 2000 Worlds the homepage linked:

* [[Matt Sokol]] Light ''Hidden Base'' and Dark ''ISB''
* [[Yannick Lapointe]] Light '''''The Machine Killa''''' and Dark '''''The Machine'''''

Those Lapointe nicknames are the published labels on this database. The transcribed 60s on this wiki dest Sokol as Hidden Base / ISB Operations and Lapointe as Mind What You Have Learned / Bring Him Before Me.

For the [[2000 European Championship]] the homepage listed [[Martin Akesson]] (Sweden) with decks '''Missing''', and Maarten Rousseau (Netherlands) with all fields '''Missing'''. This wiki dests the runner-up as [[Maarten Rossou]] from Decipher Deck Designs; the Blessed Souls spelling is Rousseau as published on that homepage.

== Preservation ==

* Homepage HTML: Wayback <code>id_</code> of t.co/RCNHte1tcY, 14 November 2020.<ref name="tco" />
* Live URL named in that post: [http://blessed-souls.mine.sk/ http://blessed-souls.mine.sk/]
* Year pages, 2000 Worlds deck HTML, and player movie/picture subpages were not captured.

Championship winners for 2002–2006 on this wiki dest from the Players Committee Awards and Hall of Fame page. Blessed Souls keywords match those names through 2005; they are not the source used for those World Championship hubs.
